items.title: Phase 1 Trial of LY4257496 in GRPR-Positive Advanced Cancers Including Prostate
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing a new drug called LY4257496 that targets a protein called GRPR found in several cancers including prostate cancer. The study is evaluating safety and effectiveness of the drug alone and combined with standard treatments. This is a phase 1 study, meaning it's the earliest stage of testing in humans to find safe doses.

items.title: Phase 1 CAR-T Cell Therapy BPX-601 for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study will test BPX-601, a CAR-T cell therapy made from patients' own immune cells, for treating advanced prostate cancer that has spread and is resistant to treatment. The trial will determine safe doses and evaluate side effects and effectiveness. CAR-T therapy is an immunotherapy approach that engineers a patient's T-cells to attack cancer. The trial has not yet started enrolling patients.

items.title: Phase 1 Trial of AMG 509 in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This trial is evaluating AMG 509, a new drug being tested alone and combined with standard hormone therapies (abiraterone and enzalutamide) for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is examining safety, side effects, how the body processes the drug, and early signs of effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients for specific study parts.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study is testing ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone and combined with other treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial aims to find safe dose levels, assess tolerability, and measure PSA response as an indicator of effectiveness. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Comparing PSMA PET Versus Bone PET Imaging in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial compares two imaging techniques for detecting metastatic prostate cancer: 18F-DCFPyL PSMA-PET versus 18F-NaF bone PET. The study evaluates which method better identifies cancer sites in patients with metastatic disease. The trial is no longer recruiting new patients but is still active.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial of TRC003 for PSMA-Positive Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This study is testing TRC003 injection in patients with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have previously received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The trial will evaluate safety, how the body processes the drug, and effectiveness across three different dose levels. Currently recruiting 90 participants.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) to standard chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. The primary goal is to determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and have longer time before cancer progression compared to those receiving chemotherapy. This is a pivotal late-stage trial that could change treatment standards.

items.title: Immunotherapy Combination for Rare Genitourinary Tumors Including Prostate
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a combination of cabozantinib (targeted therapy) with two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) for rare genitourinary tumors. While it includes some prostate cancer patients, it focuses on rare tumor types without other treatment options. The combination aims to help the immune system attack cancer while blocking tumor growth signals.

items.title: Real-World Study of Darolutamide Plus Hormone Therapy in Germany
items.summary: This observational study tracks how well darolutamide combined with standard hormone therapy (ADT) works in everyday German clinical practice for men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study observes routine treatment rather than testing an experimental approach. It will provide real-world data on effectiveness and side effects.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Trial of TD001 ADC for PSMA-Positive Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This study is evaluating TD001, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting PSMA, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial will assess safety, tolerability, drug levels in the body, and early signs of tumor response. TD001 delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells expressing PSMA protein.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: AZD2265 Versus Standard Care in PSMA-Positive Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial compares AZD2265 to standard treatments for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with PSMA-positive tumors. The study aims to prove AZD2265 is superior by measuring time until cancer progression and overall survival. This is a pivotal late-stage trial that could establish a new treatment option.

items.title: Radiation Therapy for Recurrent Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether shorter courses of radiation therapy (proton beam or IMRT) are safe and effective for prostate cancer that has returned after surgery or has spread to a limited number of sites. The study compares different radiation schedules to find approaches with fewer side effects while maintaining effectiveness.

items.title: Olaparib With or Without Cediranib for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This randomized phase 2 trial compares olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus combined with cediranib in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. PARP inhibitors prevent cancer cells from repairing DNA damage, while cediranib blocks tumor blood vessel growth. The study evaluates if the combination improves outcomes over single-drug treatment.

items.title: Phase 1 Trial of INR731 With or Without Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This phase 1 study evaluates INR731, a new oral drug, used alone or combined with standard hormone therapies (ARPIs) for metastatic prostate cancer. The trial will determine safe doses, assess side effects, measure drug levels in the body, and look for early signs of tumor response. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Versus Enzalutamide Alone
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial tests whether adding mevrometostat to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who haven't previously received hormone inhibitors or chemotherapy. This is a pivotal trial that could establish a new first-line combination treatment approach.

items.title: PDS01ADC With Docetaxel or Abiraterone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests PDS01ADC (an antibody-drug conjugate) combined with docetaxel chemotherapy and abiraterone hormone therapy for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, and PDS01ADC with docetaxel for castration-resistant disease. The study evaluates safety and effectiveness of these combinations. Currently recruiting patients.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Opevesostat Versus Alternative Hormone Therapy After One NHA
items.summary: This large phase 3 study compares opevesostat (plus hormone replacement) to switching to alternative hormone therapy (abiraterone or enzalutamide) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed on one prior hormone treatment. The trial measures time to cancer progression, with special attention to patients with AR mutations. This could establish a new treatment sequence option.

items.title: Phase 2/3 Trial: AAA817 Versus Standard Care After Lu-177-PSMA Therapy
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial tests AAA817 versus standard treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have progressed after receiving Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy. The study addresses an important clinical question about what works after PSMA therapy fails. This could establish treatment options for this challenging patient population.

items.title: Nivolumab Plus Docetaxel and ADT for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a combination of immunotherapy (nivolumab), chemotherapy (docetaxel), and hormone therapy for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in patients with specific genetic features (DNA damage repair defects) or inflamed tumors. The study evaluates if adding immunotherapy to standard treatment improves outcomes in selected patients.

items.title: Phase 3 Trial: Lu-177-PSMA Versus Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Pluvicto) PSMA radioligand therapy versus observation alone in patients with oligometastatic prostate cancer (limited metastases) after their primary tumor was treated. The study evaluates if early PSMA therapy can delay disease progression and postpone the need for hormone therapy while preserving quality of life.

items.title: Review: Successes and Limitations of PSMA Radioligand Therapy
items.summary: This medical review discusses Lu-177 PSMA radioligand therapy from a nuclear medicine perspective, highlighting its success in patient selection and rapid symptom relief, particularly for pain. However, it notes that despite good initial responses, cancer almost always returns eventually, with only modest survival benefits in trials. The review calls for more research on addressing disease recurrence and resistance.

items.title: Phase 1 Trial: Adding Lu-177-PSMA to Standard Radiation for N1 Prostate Cancer
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tested adding Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy to standard external radiation and hormone therapy for prostate cancer with lymph node spread but no distant metastases. The study found no serious toxicities and successfully determined safe dosing. This approach aims to improve cure rates by treating both visible and microscopic disease simultaneously.

items.title: Review: Combining Enzalutamide With Lu-177-PSMA Therapy
items.summary: This review article discusses the relationship between androgen receptors and PSMA in prostate cancer, explaining why combining hormone therapy (particularly enzalutamide) with PSMA radioligand therapy may improve outcomes. It introduces the ENZA-p trial, which is testing whether adding enzalutamide to Lu-177-PSMA therapy enhances treatment effectiveness in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: 2025 Advances in Radiopharmaceutical Therapy for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review summarizes major developments in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer during 2025. It discusses the evolution from radium-223 for bone-targeted pain relief to PSMA-targeted therapies that can extend survival. The field has rapidly expanded with new imaging and treatment options becoming available for metastatic prostate cancer.

items.title: Terbium-161-PSMA Therapy After Lu-177-PSMA Progression
items.summary: This study evaluated 15 metastatic CRPC patients who received Tb-161-PSMA therapy after their cancer progressed on Lu-177-PSMA treatment. Terbium-161 emits different types of radiation that may be more effective. The research provides early evidence on safety and effectiveness of this alternative radioligand when Lu-177-PSMA stops working, addressing an important clinical need.

items.title: Radium-223 After Lu-177-PSMA Therapy: Safety and Outcomes
items.summary: This retrospective study examined 21 metastatic CRPC patients who received Radium-223 bone-targeted therapy after their Lu-177-PSMA treatment. Only 19% completed all planned cycles, mostly stopping due to disease progression or blood toxicity. The study found concerning rates of severe anemia and low platelet counts, important safety information for sequencing these therapies.

items.title: Lu-177-PSMA Therapy in Treatment-Naive Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This retrospective study evaluated Lu-177-PSMA radioligand therapy in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients who had not yet received standard hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The research examines whether using PSMA therapy earlier in the disease course, before standard treatments, shows benefit. This represents an investigational approach to using PSMA therapy much earlier than currently approved.

items.title: Novel Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Treatment Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a new drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks two cancer-promoting pathways: BRD4 and AKT. This dual-targeting approach addresses a key problem where AKT inhibitors alone often fail because cancer cells develop resistance through increased c-MYC expression. Laboratory studies show this strategy may overcome resistance mechanisms in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
